newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges up, cargoes trade weaker.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges up, cargoes trade weaker.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel barges rose on Monday as one trading house was reported to be having problems with deliveries, while cargoes weakened with Russian avails and a shut arb to the United States weighing on the market, traders said.

A 1,000-tonne barge of high sulphur fuel oil traded at $87.50 a tonne fob Rotterdam after two earlier trades at $87, the same as Friday's levels. Dealers said that barges firmed as one trading house had problems delivering fuel oil and would only supply at the end of a 48-hour nomination periods. However, the trading house said it had no problems with deliveries or distribution. "That was only 1,000 tonnes but it was a genuine trade (at $87.50)," the buyer said.

"If you need prompt refinery material it is tough to get a hold of...It looks like there is no prompt tightness but you try, when everyone is putting stuff on 48 hours, it's much harder than some people think," a trader said.
Late bids were in the $85/$86 region and sellers were offering at $87/$88.
Low sulphur barges were reportedly quiet but traders said a deal was done on Friday at a slightly firmer $95 fob Rotterdam. This compares with two barge trades at $94.75 a few days earlier.

High sulphur cargoes were weaker with a small cargo of cracked material reported sold by a U.K refiner to a Rotterdam trader at $82 cif. This follows a deal on Friday for U.K. utility material at $81.75 cif.

High sulphur cargoes were talked in the $85/$86 cif region last week. One trading house was still offering its cargo at $79 fob and a second trader that was showing a cargo last week at $81/$82 said it was not offering today.
"High sulphur is a bit weakish, except on barges," one trader said.

"High sulphur should come down as we see that the arb to the States is closed. And the (Russian) M-100 that comes into the market will be available for the barge market and for buyers on the cargo market," a second trader said.
He said three to four cargoes of M-100 sold into Northwest Europe last week "amounts to about 100,000 tonnes of good quality material that can be mixed with lower quality stuff".

One percent was reportedly a dry market after a U.K. refiner was said to have sold a 75,000 tonne cargo at an attractive $94.75 a tonne fob to a trading house, which was reportedly adding some 50,000 tonnes of material to it and taking the material to Italy or Israel.
"The market looks pretty dry in one percent after Friday's deal," one trader said. Bids and offers were far apart late last week at $92/$96.
